la:noun:tectum.html:
tectum, i, n.
tego
.
Lit., a covering.
A roof: quojus (villae) Deturbavit ventus tectum ac tegulas,: de tecto deturbavit tegulas,. tecta domorum, ; : firma tecta in domiciliis habere,; cf.: disturbata porticus Catuli, quae ad tectum paene pervenerat,: hic se praecipitem tecto dedit,: culmina tecti,: tecti a culmine,.—
A ceiling (usu. plain; opp. lacunar, a fretted ceiling): tectis caelatis, laqueatis, ceilings, rooms, Enn. ap. ; (Trag. v. 121 Vahl.); cf.: qui marmoreis tectis ebore et auro fulgentibus abundant,; so, aurata,: laqueata,: cubilia tectaque,canopies,. —
Transf., a roofed building for dwelling in, a roof, house, dwelling, abode; a cover, shelter, quarters, etc. (freq. and class.; cf.: prosa, ut mucronem pro gladio, et tectum pro domo recipiet, etc.,; syn.: domus, aedes, habitatio): recipe me in tectum,; cf.: exercitus tectis ac sedibus suis recipere,: ne tecto recipiatur ... qui non, etc.,; : exercitatissimi in armis, qui inter annos XIV. tectum non subissent,: milites in tecta Gallorum contegit, Auct. B. G. 8, 5: vos, Quirites, in vestra tecta discedite,: tectis, juvenes, succedite nostris,: ejusmodi conjunctionem tectorum oppidum vel urbem appellaverunt,; : tum erat ager incultus sine tecto: nunc est cultissimus cum optimā villā,: si vacuum tepido cepisset villula tecto,: pars densa ferarum Tecta rapit silvas,: columba plausum Dat tecto ingentem,: solidis Clauditur in tectis,i. e. in prison,: sed quercus tecta cibumque dabat,: dolos tecti ambagesque resolvit, i. e. of the Labyrinth, : sub tecta Sibyllae,.

la:noun:tector.html:
tector, ōris, m.
tego
,
one that overlays walls with plaster, stucco, etc., a plasterer, pargeter: villa tua, quam neque pictor neque tector vidit umquam,; ; ; ; ; ; .

la:adj:tectorius.html:
tectōrĭus, a, um, adj.
tego
,
of or belonging to covering or to a cover.
In gen. (very rare): paniculum,thatch,. — Hence,
Subst.: tectō-rĭum, ii, n., a covering, cover, . —
In partic., that belongs to or serves for covering or overlaying walls, ceilings, floors, etc.; of or belonging to staining, painting, stuccoing, plastering, etc. (freq. and class.): opus,; cf. : neque id (sepulcrum) opere tectorio exornari,: atramentum tectorium, that serves for staining or washing walls, : saetae e penicillis tectoriis, plasterers' brushes, .—Hence,
Subst.: tec-tōrĭum, ii, n., plaster, stucco, fresco-painting, a wash for walls, etc.: parietes ac camarae munitae tectorio,; ; ; ; ; , sq.; 5, 10; ; ; ; ; . — Satirically, a paste of flour put on the face to preserve the beauty of the complexion: tandem aperit vultum et tectoria prima reponit,cover, coating,.—
Trop., of speech, smooth words, flattery (very rare): dignoscere cautus, Quid solidum crepet et pictae tectoria linguae,; so imitated, ad Volusian.

senses: plaster, stucco, fresco-painting, a wash for walls
